chapterName: PS & EAM (topics mentioned in the textbook)

topics.topicName: PS – Project System concepts in the textbook

questions.question: Which controlling object is described as relevant to project management?
questions.explanation: In the order of priority for real postings: profitability segment, make-to-order sales order, WBS element, internal order, cost center.

questions.question: In the order of priority for real postings in controlling, where does the WBS element rank?

options.A: Third: after the profitability segment and the make-to-order sales order, and before the internal order and cost center
options.D: Second, directly after the cost center

questions.explanation: The order is profitability segment, make-to-order sales order, WBS element, internal order, cost center.

questions.question: Which objects other than cost centers can be designated as statistical objects when they are created?
questions.explanation: Profit centers are statistical objects by definition.

questions.question: Projects can be receivers of costs in which allocation techniques?

options.B: Distribution and assessment (periodic allocation), and internal activity allocation
options.D: None; projects can never be receivers

questions.explanation: Valid receivers include several real objects such as internal orders, projects and maintenance orders; internal activity allocation can charge production orders and projects.

questions.question: Which production process is most often applied in constructing a facility or manufacturing an item such as an aircraft that requires a complex production process?
questions.explanation: The job shop process is used for highly customized items such as a custom motorcycle.

questions.question: What do the job shop and project production processes focus on?

options.A: A desired production rate such as units per day
options.B: A single item (project) or a highly customized item or items (job shop)
options.C: Materials that are indistinguishable from their components

questions.explanation: Repetitive production specifies a rate; discrete production specifies a quantity.

questions.question: Which sales scenario is a make-to-order scenario that is relevant to controlling postings (priority just above WBS element)?
questions.explanation: Make-to-order is triggered by an actual customer order.

topics.topicName: EAM – Enterprise Asset Management concepts in the textbook

questions.question: The costs of repairing equipment (materials, labor) are accumulated in which object in the enterprise asset management process?
questions.explanation: EAM is used to repair equipment; the repair costs accumulate in the maintenance order.

questions.question: When the maintenance process is completed, to which receiver are the accumulated costs typically settled?

options.A: The vendor who supplied the spare parts
options.B: The customer who ordered the repair
options.C: The cost center that owns the equipment

questions.explanation: Settlement applies to other management accounting processes, not only to internal orders.

questions.question: Which technique transfers the costs accumulated in a maintenance order to a controlling object?
questions.explanation: Settlement uses settlement rules, parameters and profiles.

questions.question: Which allocation structure in the example is for enterprise asset management?
questions.explanation: A3 is for customer service; Z1 for internal orders; A1 and A2 are general structures.

questions.question: Can maintenance orders function as valid receivers in a distribution?

options.A: No, only cost centers can be receivers
options.B: Yes, together with other real objects such as internal orders and projects
options.C: No, only G/L accounts can be receivers

questions.explanation: Only cost centers are valid senders in a distribution or assessment.

questions.question: Which financial accounting-related process step generates costs that flow into management accounting, including the cost of repairs to machinery?

options.C: Period closing of balance sheet accounts
options.D: Asset management (maintenance), alongside asset accounting and procurement

questions.explanation: Costs originate in postings of processes such as asset accounting (depreciation), procurement (supplies) and asset management (repairs).

questions.question: For which processes can bills of materials be created, according to the textbook?

options.B: Production, product costing and enterprise asset management

questions.explanation: The BOM application parameter indicates which type of BOM may be used in production.

questions.question: For which purposes are routings used, according to the textbook?

options.A: Production, asset management and quality inspections

questions.explanation: The routing selection parameter also indicates whether routing is mandatory or optional.

questions.question: For which application areas are work center categories assigned?

options.C: Application areas such as production and maintenance, which determine the types of routings (task lists) that can be assigned

questions.explanation: Work centers are used in many processes including production and asset management.
